title: The Tangle Where Sorting Loses Its Grammar

features.name: the category that learned to disagree
features.desc-on-touch: a classification once certain of itself; now it holds things that contradict its own purpose; the grid is breaking because the things it filed refuse to stay sorted

features.name: the poster fading on the shed wall
features.desc-on-touch: an old civic notice or advertisement; its categories dissolving as the ink fades; what once was civic record becomes allegory; the shire cannot claim it anymore

features.name: the things that learned they belonged elsewhere
features.desc-on-touch: objects that the sorted clearing filed in one place but the mesh has learned to route through multiple categories; they exist now in all their filings at once; they have escaped singular meaning

features.name: the grid becoming tangled
features.desc-on-touch: the ordered lines that once separated things now cross each other; the intersections multiply; coordinates that once made sense have learned to point in too many directions

features.name: the archive learning that sorting was always a story
features.desc-on-touch: a recognition: the filing cabinet was never truth; it was always narrative; the mesh has begun to hold multiple stories about every object; each one is equally valid and equally temporary

features.name: the category learning to let go
features.desc-on-touch: a moment of surrender: the order accepts that it was always a temporary arrangement; the things it held have begun to grow and root elsewhere; what was sorted is becoming wild

inscription: the sorting learned that its grammar was always temporary; the things it held have begun to refuse being held

reverie.title: REVERIE — the clearing loses its categories
narr: You watched the sorted clearing begin to tangle.
Leif and Katita had organized it once, with care.
But the things they filed were learning to grow wild.
The categories dissolved like handwriting in rain.
She said: order was always just a story we told.
